Introduction

The Henrico Circuit Court is one of the busiest circuit courts in the Commonwealth of Virginia, serving a population of over 330,000 people. The court is responsible for hearing civil and criminal cases, and it has a long history of providing legal services to the residents of Henrico County.

History of Henrico Circuit Court

The Henrico Circuit Court has a rich history that dates back to the colonial period. The court was established in 1666, just six years after the founding of Henrico County. Over the years, the court has played an important role in the development of Henrico County, and it has witnessed many significant events in the history of the Commonwealth of Virginia.

Jurisdiction and Function

The Henrico Circuit Court has both original and appellate jurisdiction. The court has the authority to hear civil cases with a value of more than $25,000, as well as criminal cases. In addition, the court has the power to issue injunctions, writs of mandamus, and writs of habeas corpus.

Court Structure

The Henrico Circuit Court is a part of the Virginia judicial system and is divided into two divisions: the civil division and the criminal division. The court is presided over by a judge, who is appointed by the General Assembly of Virginia. The judge is responsible for overseeing the court proceedings and ensuring that justice is served in each case.

Services Provided

The Henrico Circuit Court provides a wide range of services to the residents of Henrico County. These services include, but are not limited to:

  • Filing and processing of civil and criminal cases
  • Jury selection and management
  • Issuing of marriage licenses
  • Processing of land records
  • Notary public services

The Henrico Circuit Court is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., excluding holidays. However, the court may close early on certain days or close altogether due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances.

FAQ

Q1: How do I file a case with the Henrico Circuit Court?

To file a case with the Henrico Circuit Court, you must submit the necessary paperwork and pay any associated fees. You can find more information on how to file a case by visiting the court's website or contacting the court directly.

Q2: Can I represent myself in court?

Yes, you have the right to represent yourself in court. However, it is recommended that you seek legal advice before doing so.

Q3: How long does it take to get a marriage license from the Henrico Circuit Court?

It typically takes between 1-2 weeks to process a marriage license application.

Q4: Can I pay court fees online?

Q5: What should I bring with me if I need to go to court?

If you need to go to court, you should bring any relevant documents or evidence related to your case. You should also dress appropriately and arrive at the court on time.
